Information since May points to a strong labor market and moderate growth—consistent with Okun’s law linking lower unemployment to stronger real activity, and with New Keynesian policy frameworks (e.g., Clarida–Galí–Gertler) where real activity and inflation expectations guide the policy rate through rules like the Taylor rule. This mix signals a constructive, but not exuberant, macro backdrop that would typically justify a cautious policy stance.
